name: ZeroBrain integration
purpose: Connect the operator's views, work lanes, research, authority and evidence without treating the coordinator as the whole project.
inputs: Operator intent; coordinator and knowledge APIs; work and review state.
outputs: An integrated view and interaction boundary across COHORT.
owner: An integration boundary with no database of its own. Durable facts stay with their owning services.
boundary: The exported guides map part of its implementation boundary, and this atlas shows only what they document.
runtime: Documented subsystem; the coordinator and related services run outside this snapshot.

name: MCP / REST coordinator
purpose: Give cooperating sessions one authenticated place to route work, messages, identity, authority and accepted transitions.
inputs: Node bootstrap; MCP tools; REST requests; task/review/lifecycle actions.
outputs: Authenticated results, durable transitions and dashboard/event projections.
owner: Coordinator records own live fleet state and operational actions.
boundary: Completion comes from the owning record, so a message, heartbeat or frontend success indicator never counts on its own. Exact protected actions go through their backend gates.
runtime: Documented FastAPI/MCP contracts; server implementation and running service are external.

name: Operational write-of-record
purpose: Keep tasks, claims, identity, reviews, authority, messages and incident evidence from becoming competing local versions of truth.
inputs: Accepted coordinator writes and lifecycle transitions.
outputs: Durable state, audits and API projections.
owner: Coordinator relational records; PostgreSQL is the documented production substrate, SQLite the test/legacy path.
boundary: Storage backend and logical record ownership are different questions. Do not infer a table's database from a cairn_ name prefix.
runtime: Database/schema contracts documented; no populated database or database service bundled.

name: Cairn durable knowledge
aliases: RFC, seed, scratch and KB persistence
purpose: Preserve proposals, research, rationale, revisions and decisions so later work can inspect why a design exists.
inputs: Seeds, RFC bodies, responses, signals, syntheses and knowledge records.
outputs: Content-addressed revisions, lifecycle/audit records and source material for search.
owner: Cairn's durable records; the guides distinguish its knowledge store from coordinator operational records.
boundary: The enforced stage is ideation, which replaced the stale rfc alias. Ratified content is guarded, and changes follow the documented revision and authority path.
runtime: Documented persistence/contracts; no Cairn backend or data service bundled.

name: Spyglass research and search
aliases: Project Spyglass; derived SQLite / FTS5 index
purpose: Make research and knowledge discoverable without letting search size or corruption control the primary store.
inputs: Indexed RFC, seed, KB, scratch, SWAT and lesson content; tags/provenance.
outputs: Search snippets, relevance-ranked results, tags and index statistics.
owner: Derived index only. Verify a retrieved result against its Cairn/source record before treating it as current guidance.
boundary: Source-to-index is one-way; corruption is quarantined and rebuilt with a bounded budget, never a reason to erase durable source rows.
runtime: Search contracts documented; the demo filters invented records with a simple stand-in for FTS5 and the Spyglass engine.

name: RFC design proposals
aliases: Waves; responses; signals; PM synthesis; SOLIDPLAN
purpose: Turn a proposal and the team's input, objections included, into a design the team can build from.
inputs: Proposal body and revision, adoption plan, each node's responses and reactions, the PM synthesis and any cited approvals.
outputs: seed -> ideation -> in_round -> ratified -> shipped; append-only lifecycle audit and a ratify binding.
owner: Cairn. A wave is a round of team input; building and delivery come later through tasks.
boundary: Each node weighs in from its role and the work it usually leads. The PM's summary of each round carries the most weight, and the operator has the final say on approving the design as ready to build. There's no head count, and every response stays on the record.
runtime: Contracts documented; original lifecycle/wave display helpers are included, and backend enforcement runs outside this snapshot.

name: RFC vessel-host Council
purpose: Challenge an RFC through different perspectives without printing the same shared assumptions five times.
inputs: Verbatim body and framing question; outsider, first-principles, executor, expansionist and contrarian lenses.
outputs: Verbatim considerations appended under an audited firing record.
owner: Cairn firing/revision records. The vessel transports and captures output while the lenses respond.
boundary: The RFC author and prior vessels are excluded from hosting; context stripping, canary/version checks and append-only capture protect independence.
runtime: Documented agent-orchestrated mechanism; no lens sessions are launched by this site.

name: Response-level LSG council
purpose: Annotate individual responses through distinct adversarial, invariant and provenance lenses.
inputs: A response; devils_advocate, invariant_checker and provenance_honesty lenses.
outputs: Structured per-response/lens annotations with severity.
owner: Cairn council annotation records, kept apart from the RFC vessel-host firing table.
boundary: The guides describe two unrelated council mechanisms. They share a name, and each has its own invariants and execution.
runtime: Documented worker contract; worker implementation/runtime absent.

name: Research / KB / scratch lifecycle
aliases: Knowledge triage; source pointers; living references
purpose: Keep useful evidence and operating doctrine discoverable without treating every note as a ratified commitment.
inputs: Observations, research-shaped material, scratch evidence, doctrine and superseded records.
outputs: Knowledge records, candidates, pointer stubs and labeled historical material.
owner: Cairn owns current doctrine and provenance; Spyglass can carry indexed long-form research with source pointers.
boundary: Do not move load-bearing contracts or prohibitions out of their authoritative source for search convenience.
runtime: Documented lifecycle and triage policy; no actual research corpus is published in the sample.

name: Session continuity search
purpose: Retrieve handoff/event context while respecting whose session history a caller may inspect.
inputs: Session handoff and event records, with noisy heartbeat events excluded.
outputs: Identity-scoped search snippets.
owner: The handoff/event sources remain authoritative; this is a separate derived FTS5 index.
boundary: Access is identity-gated, and token-shaped secrets are kept out of snippets. The research/KB index is a separate system.
runtime: Documented separate search contract; no real sessions or history included.

name: Kanban tasks and work claims
purpose: Prevent duplicate work and keep implementation progress separate from design decisions.
inputs: Routed build work, task dependencies, claims, implementation evidence and review acknowledgements.
outputs: ready -> in_progress -> review -> done, with accepted ownership and closure.
owner: Coordinator task records. Dashboard cards and message order are views of them.
boundary: Losing a claim race costs nothing in work-in-progress. Scope determines the lane, so only new cross-system designs need an RFC.
runtime: Contracts documented; the included task-board renderer demonstrates with invented objects.

name: Swatter targeted-fix lane
aliases: SWAT; observation, fix and closure state machine
purpose: Give a narrow defect a specific owner, verdict and closure path instead of forcing it into a large design process.
inputs: Targeted observations, design input where needed, fix citations, reviewer verdicts and dispositions.
outputs: open -> in_review -> fixed -> closed, or explicit changes/rejection/refile outcomes.
owner: Coordinator Swatter rows; they stay in the coordinator despite the cairn_ prefix.
boundary: Design input is always considered. Author/prior-reviewer/cluster/design-input recusal is lane-specific, and unknown ancestry stays visible until verification runs.
runtime: Documented state machine; reference UI included, backend absent.

name: Boomerang work transport
purpose: Move a piece of work to an appropriate recipient without inventing another durable work owner.
inputs: Routable tasks/SWATs and return verdicts.
outputs: Recipient handoffs and atomic write-back through the owning lane.
owner: Transport only; Swatter/task records own their lifecycle.
boundary: Re-routing excludes prior reviewers and escalates exhausted pools, which prevents reviewer ping-pong.
runtime: Contracts and preserved frontend code available; no transport backend is bundled.

name: Independent artifact review
purpose: Prevent approval of one revision from being applied to another, or an author's claim from replacing independent evidence.
inputs: Artifact/base/head relationship, eligible reviewer, verdict, notes and required acceptance evidence.
outputs: Recorded acknowledgements/verdicts that let the owning task or SWAT advance.
owner: Coordinator review records and the owning work lane.
boundary: Strict task ancestry mismatches are rejected; non-strict mismatches are audited. Depth rises for vital runtime/lifecycle changes. Authorization and completion are separate steps after review.
runtime: Review contracts documented; original review table renderer included, enforcement/runtime absent.

name: Operator authority / OPA
aliases: Directives, bounded grants, role and task gates
purpose: Keep a legitimate request, permission to perform it and acceptance of its result from becoming one ambiguous signal.
inputs: Captured operator directive; identity; role; scope; delegation chain; expiring or action-scoped grant.
outputs: Accepted/rejected privileged action and audit evidence.
owner: Coordinator authority records. OPA grants bounded elevation, and review and evidence still apply.
boundary: Unknown or out-of-scope authority needs a new decision. Irreversible/PM-only paths may disallow elevation; undocumented auth labels remain explicit gaps.
runtime: Contracts documented; no keys, sessions or authorization service in the public site.

name: Messages / outbox / event streams
purpose: Deliver actionable communication and invalidate derived views without treating notification order as ownership.
inputs: Authenticated messages; lifecycle/outbox events; substantive responses and acknowledgements.
outputs: Inbox state, event projections and dashboard refresh triggers.
owner: Coordinator message/outbox records; frontend notification queues are derived.
boundary: Process actionable content before acknowledgement. Degraded SSE/poll fallback is labeled, and work completes through its owning record.
runtime: Contracts and preserved client code available; no message/event service runs in Pages.

name: Manual mode / TotemTask
aliases: Explicit wake; work chunks; proof receipts
purpose: Avoid recurring idle prompt cost while retaining task ownership, authority and completion evidence.
inputs: Explicit wake, PM-authored work chunk and authoritative coordinator actions.
outputs: Executed chunk, node-owned append-only proof and PM reconciliation.
owner: The plan coordinates assignment; accepted coordinator actions still own task/SWAT/review closure.
boundary: Scheduled prompting is suspended and shown as suspended. Proof is written after the owning action succeeds. The three durable work lanes stay unchanged.
runtime: Documented operating model; no wake/schedule/launcher runs in the demo.

name: Agent runtime / MCP integration
aliases: Copilot CLI node; direct or bridged MCP mode
purpose: Give each engineering role an isolated execution environment connected to the coordinator.
inputs: Node-local configuration, startup instructions, model/context settings and a verified runtime/bridge.
outputs: A node session that can perform authenticated tools and preserve continuity.
owner: Local runtime artifacts configure execution; coordinator identity and durable work are still authoritative.
boundary: Each shared-host node keeps its own CLI home and process tree. Binary/bridge policy and bounded retry protect launch assumptions.
runtime: Rebuild contracts only; CLI nodes, bridge binaries and the launcher harness run outside this snapshot.

name: Fleet boot / bootstrap
purpose: Start the right node with the right identity and recover it without inheriting a neighbor's session.
inputs: Persistent local identity, canonical startup template, per-node MCP configuration and bootstrap authentication.
outputs: Session-token continuity, generated node artifacts and post-boot verification.
owner: Identity/configuration and coordinator bootstrap records; generated files are mirrors.
boundary: Resolve paths from the node's own identity; keep secrets out of generated source and logs. Manual mode changes the post-boot loop and leaves authentication as is.
runtime: Documented boot chain; launcher implementation/runtime external.

name: Fleet topology / service discovery
purpose: Make co-tenant safety and service location explicit before restart, launch or vital changes.
inputs: Generic host roles, service identities and approved topology/profile relationships.
outputs: Static reachability/placement references used by runtime and review.
owner: Fleet Topology is the static reference; coordinator state describes live fleet observations.
boundary: Static placement says where a node should be, and liveness needs its own check. Vital launch review requires topology/profile-isolation evidence for the actual host.
runtime: Contract only; no real infrastructure roster or host addresses are published.

name: Identity / session tokens
purpose: Distinguish who a node is, what it is allowed to do and what it has actually earned.
inputs: Operator-controlled startup fields, authenticated bootstrap, evidence-derived competencies and factual session summary.
outputs: Resolved caller identity, bounded token continuity and audited corrections.
owner: Coordinator identity/session records plus the node's persistent configuration.
boundary: Session token outranks IP fallback. Competence is awarded by others, and corrections stay on the record.
runtime: Documented identity contract; no real identity/session data in the public sample.

name: Typed durable memory
purpose: Keep useful bounded context available after the current conversation or process disappears.
inputs: Self-owned factual memory writes and revisions.
outputs: Typed blocks, revision audit and point-in-time rollback.
owner: Coordinator memory rows/audit. They hold context, while work completion and authority have their own records.
boundary: Overflow fails loudly, so nothing is truncated silently. Durable context informs later work.
runtime: Memory contracts documented; no memory service or actual personal session content bundled.

name: Session handoff
aliases: Typed commitments; primary head pointer; successor context
purpose: Prevent a successor from receiving a vague promise instead of the concrete work and rationale it must resume.
inputs: Self-authored head pointers, typed in-flight commitments and subject references.
outputs: Bounded preview/finalized handoff with staleness checks.
owner: Coordinator session-handoff records, separate from KB/RFC knowledge.
boundary: A handoff says what to resume; task completion and authority stay with their owners. Saving happens before any destructive session replacement.
runtime: Documented continuity contract; handoff backend absent.

name: Engineering roles / personas
aliases: Architect, PM, builders, reviewers and analyst perspectives
purpose: Give the team six distinct voices, each asking deliberately different questions.
inputs: Role authority, startup templates, authored temperament and durable corrections/context.
outputs: Complementary engineering perspectives and continuity templates.
owner: Role definitions and persona documents; authenticated runtime identity remains a different contract.
boundary: Personality is a design and interaction aid. Gary is a disposable specification, separate from the role personas.
runtime: Persona/template documents included; no active team is running in Pages.

name: Molt / controlled refresh
purpose: Replace a session without losing its obligations or killing a co-tenant by accident.
inputs: Saved context/handoff, dwell/moratorium/authority checks, topology and verified refresh artifact.
outputs: Controlled transition and observed successor verification.
owner: Coordinator lifecycle state and persistent identity/handoff; the launcher is an execution mechanism.
boundary: A planned replacement with post-fire verification. Known context-freshness caveats stay visible.
runtime: Protocol/rebuild contracts only; refresh scripts/runtime are external.

name: Breathbus daemon
purpose: Provide a liveness substrate distinct from the agent's scheduled prompt loop or its completed work.
inputs: Daemon/runtime observations and topology configuration.
outputs: Breathing/liveness observations consumed by coordinator and dashboard surfaces.
owner: Infrastructure observations. Live coordinator state, durable work and task completion each stay with their own records.
boundary: A running daemon shows the bus is up. Scheduled prompt polling and agent attention are tracked separately.
runtime: Documented infrastructure contract; the daemon implementation runs outside this snapshot.

name: Automated bb4-poll contract
aliases: Scheduled prompts; batched inbox and heartbeat
purpose: Wake and check an agent on an explicitly authorized automated cadence.
inputs: Enabled schedule, inbox work, heartbeat and substantive message processing.
outputs: Ordered batch/acknowledgement behavior and liveness signals.
owner: Coordinator mode/schedule and message records. Productive work is measured by its own records.
boundary: Manual mode suspends this loop. An expensive work obligation needs the work itself, and a heartbeat or acknowledgement leaves it open.
runtime: Opt-in automated-mode contract only; no schedule is active in the public site.

name: Out-of-band health / Failure Episodes
aliases: External watchdog; durable degraded/recovered incident stream
purpose: Record failure evidence even when the coordinator is too wedged to report its own condition.
inputs: External UNHEALTHY/RECOVERED artifacts, ordered replay and remediation evidence.
outputs: Deduplicated episode transitions with a durable ingest cursor.
owner: Failure Episode records, kept as their own durable stream apart from RFCs, KB articles and tasks.
boundary: Ingestion is bounded and non-fatal, so an unreadable artifact never blocks startup. Unknown or degraded states always render as warnings.
runtime: Watchdog/incident backend contracts documented; original incident UI exists, no actual feed is bundled.

name: Gary disposable canary
purpose: Try risky startup and life-service instructions in an isolated, disposable process before they reach a real node.
inputs: Agent-acquired lease, candidate specification and assertions.
outputs: pass/fail/bricked verdict; agent-submitted durable result and lease release.
owner: Coordinator result/lease; the harness owns only disposable process isolation.
boundary: The harness runs without cohort identity or coordinator calls. Full ephemeral joining is a separate, unbundled slice.
runtime: Harness contract and original status UI documented; harness implementation/runtime absent.

name: Merit capability record
aliases: Role levels, nominations and award audit
purpose: Distinguish evidence-earned capabilities from aspirations or self-description.
inputs: Evidence-backed nominations and PM/operator decisions.
outputs: Role-specific badges/levels and successful/rejected change audits.
owner: Coordinator Merit records.
boundary: Self-awards are rejected. Role assignment, permission and completed work each have their own records; runtime usage is outside this map.
runtime: Contract and original frontend panel included; the backend runs outside this snapshot.

name: Durable lessons / graduation
purpose: Carry evidenced failure lessons into later context without filling boot with an unbounded history.
inputs: Subject/fact/citations/reason/scope, revisions and graduation evidence.
outputs: Bounded active lessons, current revision and best-effort Spyglass projection.
owner: Coordinator lesson records; their durable write survives an index failure.
boundary: Graduation is the quality filter. Scope privilege and the ten-item active boot cap keep lessons focused and deliberate.
runtime: Contracts and original lesson UI included; the backend runs outside this snapshot.

name: Database backup / restore
purpose: Recover the authoritative stores in full, with dashboards and loose database files as secondary concerns.
inputs: Configured backend, sanctioned maintenance authority and integrity-verified backup.
outputs: Durably published snapshot and restore evidence before writes resume.
owner: Operational and Cairn stores have their own backup paths; derived indexes/caches are rebuilt.
boundary: PostgreSQL needs a live custom-format dump and validation; SQLite backup is the test/legacy path. A recovery counts once it's verified.
runtime: Recovery contract only; no database snapshots, passwords or recovery infrastructure included.

name: Superdash frontend
purpose: Let an operator inspect tasks, research, reviews, authority, messages, lessons, incidents and runtime condition without opening every record by hand.
inputs: Coordinator/Cairn projections, API responses, outbox/SSE events and cache state.
outputs: Rendered views, credentialed actions in the reference app and visible freshness/degraded states.
owner: A derived presentation/interaction layer, never the owner of work or authorization.
boundary: Reference UI code is included and runs offline. Pages reuses selected renderers with invented data and no operational clients.
runtime: Executable frontend included; live data/actions require an external backend. Public sample is disconnected.

name: Dashboard HTTP / diagnostic server
aliases: Static assets; health/version/drift; GET proxy; SSH-lane probe
purpose: Serve the UI and let it diagnose itself even when the coordinator is unreachable.
inputs: Static files, local configuration, selected integration ref and optional coordinator GETs.
outputs: Health/version/deploy/lane observations, compressed assets and faithfully relayed upstream statuses.
owner: Local server/deploy facts only; proxied work remains coordinator-owned.
boundary: A TCP connection without an SSH banner shows as degraded. This trusted-operator reference server is separate from the public Pages runtime.
runtime: Python standard-library server and deterministic tests included; optional upstream must be supplied.

name: Optional image upload service
aliases: FastAPI image storage and SQLite metadata
purpose: Attach/share images in the connected reference dashboard.
inputs: Allowed image types, configured upload directory and required environment token.
outputs: Stored file, metadata and share link.
owner: The service's local upload files and metadata. Task and decision authority live elsewhere.
boundary: Real uploads and tokens stay private. The original service needs its own dependencies and deployment review, and it sits outside the Pages artifact.
runtime: Service source included; optional FastAPI/uvicorn/multipart dependencies and configured secret required.

name: Cache / provenance / delivery tooling
aliases: Version stamps, service worker, deploy drift, receipts
purpose: Close the gap between changing source and an operator actually receiving the new interface.
inputs: Reviewed source, served asset bytes, URL cache stamps and observed deployment state.
outputs: Content-hash lint verdicts, cache-version visibility and verified deployment receipts.
owner: Receipts and projections describe delivery; task acceptance and RFC ratification stay with their owners.
boundary: Immutable URLs require stamp changes with content. The public sample has no service worker or operational deploy controls.
runtime: Reference JS/Python/PowerShell tooling and tests included; actual site deployment uses a separate docs-only Pages workflow.

name: Historical variants / compatibility
aliases: HB lineage; legacy Molt; SQLite production-era descriptions
purpose: Preserve why a design changed without presenting retired mechanisms as rebuild targets.
inputs: Superseded protocols, archived design material and documented conflicts.
outputs: Labeled lineage and migration constraints.
owner: Historical evidence only; the current documented contract wins for new implementation.
boundary: HB3/HB4/HB5/HB6-era loops, bubble/watchers, Smooth-Molt/Swift-Molt and older remote Molt stay retired unless deliberately reactivated.
runtime: Historical documentation; no retired runtime is deployed or bundled as an active system.
